intro.title: will-change
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with a button that smoothly changes color when hovered over, using the CSS `will-change` property to optimize performance. You will learn how `will-change` hints to the browser about elements that are likely to change, allowing it to prepare resources in advance for smoother animations. The main technologies involved are CSS for styling and the `will-change` property specifically for performance optimization. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you understand when and how to apply `will-change` to improve user experience without overusing it.
intro.usecase: The `will-change` property is used by developers to optimize performance in complex, interactive user interfaces. For example, in a data dashboard with real-time updating charts or a scrolling news feed with parallax effects, applying `will-change` to the animated elements can prevent jank by hinting to the browser which properties are likely to change. This is crucial for maintaining smooth animations in product carousels, expanding side panels, or draggable modal windows, ensuring a polished user experience. By strategically using `will-change`, developers can proactively manage rendering performance in dynamic web applications.
